title: Bernie Sanders Hits Back at Sam Altman After OpenAI CEO Warns of 'Severe Cyber Incidents' in Exchange for 'Liberty': 'We Won't Accept' It
key_facts: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) called on Monday for a permanent ban on artificial superintelligence.
He was responding to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman on Politico's Decoded podcast the week before.
Altman warned of a 'coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems' and that society may 'have to just accept some fairly severe cyber incidents from open models'.
Sanders wrote on X: 'No, Mr. Altman. We won't accept a severe AI cyberattack in exchange for liberty.'
In September Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll last Wednesday found 57% of registered voters said the Trump administration was not taking AI risks seriously.
quote_evidence: "No, Mr. Altman. We won't accept a severe AI cyberattack in exchange for 'liberty,'" Sanders wrote on X.
Trump has taken a sharply different approach.
why_it_matters_hint: A senator publicly rejects the trade-off Altman described, linking the debate to a ban bill.
